summary: Iteration 31 — Force-update gate re-wiring in app/_layout.tsx. Backend: 6/6 PASS (/api/version public + /api/admin/version GET/PUT round-trip incl. admin auth + reset). Frontend: HARD-BLOCK (force_update=true) and DISMISSIBLE (force_update=false + Skip) both PASS: gate renders with correct testIDs update-gate/update-btn/update-skip, hides Skip when forced, dismisses correctly when not. TWO SIGNIFICANT ISSUES FOUND: (1) Gate incorrectly appears even when latest_version == installed (1.0.1==1.0.1) on the Expo web preview — the `installed` fallback in UpdateGateHost cannot determine the app version on web (Application.nativeApplicationVersion is null on web, and Constants.expoConfig?.version is not resolving in the built web bundle), so `installed` collapses to '0.0.0' and every comparison marks the app outdated. Confirmed by the gate text 'Please update TaskMint to v1.0.1' rendering after we reset latest_version=1.0.1. This means the 'no gate when current' case FAILS on web (and any other platform where the installed version cannot be resolved). (2) Admin exemption does NOT engage after signing in through the gate's own long-press admin escape modal: adminLogin succeeded on backend (long-press → modal → submit → 200), but the gate remained visible and the router.push('/admin/settings') ended up at /login, indicating useAuth().user.is_admin never became true (or the session flip caused the auth guard to redirect). Because of this, admins can still be locked out on web. /admin/version page loads and its form is present. Reset to latest_version=1.0.1, force_update=false, release_notes='' was performed successfully at the end (verified via /api/version). Deprecated packages: none newly introduced by this change. Regression Home/Earn/Wallet/Profile navigation was NOT verified end-to-end because the broken 'installed' detection kept the gate active on web the entire time (would only be blocked when we could sign in as admin — which failed).

ui_bugs.issue: On Expo web, `Application.nativeApplicationVersion` returns null and `Constants.expoConfig?.version` is not populated at runtime, so `installed` falls back to '0.0.0'. Result: gate is ALWAYS shown on web because 0.0.0 < any latest_version (even 1.0.1). Reproduced: set latest_version=1.0.1, force_update=false → gate still rendered with 'Please update TaskMint to v1.0.1'. Suggested fix: (a) also read version from a web-safe source (e.g. Constants.manifest2?.extra?.expoClient?.version, Constants.manifest?.version, or import app.json's version directly for web builds), and/or (b) if `installed` cannot be resolved, default to 'do not show gate' rather than '0.0.0'.

Long-press on update-btn opens admin modal, credentials submit successfully (backend returns 200 with is_admin=true on the same session), but on the frontend the gate remains visible and router.push('/admin/settings') lands the user at /login. useAuth().user.is_admin is not reflected, so UpdateGateWrapper's admin-exemption branch never triggers. Reproduced with force_update=true. Suggested check: verify AuthContext.adminLogin() refreshes `user` state (or invalidates it so /auth/me is re-fetched) synchronously before returning; also inspect the login-redirect guard for /admin/settings.

integration_issues.issue: Because installed=='0.0.0' on web, the 'no-gate when current' case cannot be observed in the Expo web preview. Real APK/IPA builds (where Application.nativeApplicationVersion is populated) are likely fine, but the web preview is broken.

Post-submit route ends at /login instead of /admin/settings and gate stays up on all admin routes (/admin/version included). Blocks the intended 'admin can always sign in and toggle force_update off' escape hatch on web.

action_items: Fix `installed` detection in /app/frontend/app/_layout.tsx (UpdateGateHost, lines ~161-165). Options: (a) add web fallback via `require('../app.json').expo.version`, or (b) if version cannot be determined, treat as 'not outdated' (return early / set installed = info.latest_version). Confirm gate is hidden when latest_version==1.0.1 on the Expo web preview.

Fix admin-login path from UpdateGate.tsx submitAdmin(): after AuthContext.adminLogin() succeeds, ensure `user.is_admin` becomes true in the AuthContext state before the Modal closes so UpdateGateWrapper.shouldShow flips to false (and router.push('/admin/settings') lands there instead of /login). Likely needs to re-fetch /auth/me or set user optimistically inside adminLogin.

After fixes, re-verify: (i) latest=1.0.1 force=false → NO gate; (ii) latest=1.0.2 force=true → hard block for non-admin, gone for admin; (iii) latest=1.0.2 force=false → dismissible; (iv) /admin/version PUT round-trip (already green in backend tests); (v) Home/Earn/Wallet/Profile boot cleanly.
critical_code_review_comments: UpdateGateHost fallback `Constants.expoConfig?.version || '0.0.0'` defaults to the WORST possible value (0.0.0 forces the gate on). Prefer defaulting to `latest_version` (no update needed) when installed cannot be determined.

UpdateGate.submitAdmin() assumes adminLogin() flips is_admin synchronously; if it does not, the gate remains visible and the escape is broken. Consider awaiting a state settle or re-fetching /auth/me before dismissing the modal.

rca_of_issue: BUG 1 root cause: `installed` fallback chain in UpdateGateHost is `Application.nativeApplicationVersion || Constants.expoConfig?.version || '0.0.0'`. On the Expo web preview both antecedents resolve falsy, so installed becomes literal '0.0.0'; `compareVersions('0.0.0','1.0.1') < 0` is true → outdated=true → gate rendered even when admin's latest_version equals the real installed 1.0.1. Fix by reading app.json's version directly for the web platform (import * as pkg from '../app.json') OR by treating an unresolved installed as 'up-to-date' (return early). BUG 2 root cause: UpdateGate.submitAdmin awaits adminLogin() but the AuthContext user state is not observably updated to is_admin=true afterwards on web, so UpdateGateWrapper's shouldShow does not go false; on top of that, router.push('/admin/settings') is bounced to /login by the auth guard, further indicating the user object is not yet admin at redirect time. Fix by ensuring adminLogin() updates the in-memory user (or re-fetches /auth/me) before resolving.
